surprises.description: Watsco reported diluted EPS of $3.77, well below the preview’s $4.11–$4.15 consensus range and $4.04 buy-side whisper. The shortfall was about 8%–9% versus consensus.

Gross margin was 26.4%, roughly 90 basis points below the preview’s ~27.3% estimate and below the 27.5% baseline investors were told to watch. Jackson Supply’s below-Watsco margins modestly weighed on the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margins of 26.4%”; Jackson Supply “operates below Watsco's ~27% margin, modestly weighing on consolidated margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: ~27.3%”; the preview called 27.5% “the baseline that we expect looking forward.”

surprises.description: Residential HVAC equipment grew 7%, with both unit volume and pricing contributing, despite the preview’s concern about weak residential volumes and its reference to a peer’s residential volume decline. New construction and multifamily were particularly strong, while replacement grew more slowly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Residential HVAC equipment…grew 7% with gains in both unit volume and pricing”; “residential new construction/multifamily rose low double digits and add-on replacement rose low single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the call would test whether “Lennox's residential volume collapse is a share-shift/OEM issue or a true end-market problem,” and noted Lennox residential volumes were “−12%.”

surprises.description: Revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s consensus range: $2.22 billion versus $2.20–$2.21 billion. The beat was small, and same-store growth of 4% was broadly consistent with the preview’s expected organic pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sales rose 7% to a record $2.22 billion (4% on a same-store basis).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $2.20–2.21B”; consensus implied “+6.4% to +6.9%” growth, with the preview estimating roughly 3.5% organic growth.

surprises.description: Management reported that October revenues were up double digits quarter-to-date and had improved sequentially month over month since May. The update is encouraging against the preview’s concern about a possible late-summer slowdown, although the October growth figure includes acquisitions and does not establish the organic trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarter-to-date October revenues are up double digits including acquisitions,” with “sequential month-over-month improvement since May.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said an October quarter-to-date organic figure was the “highest-signal datapoint” and warned that August–September volumes might roll over.

surprises.description: Watsco said it remained in a positive net cash flow position even after funding the Granite acquisition, with $649 million of cash and no debt at quarter-end. That provides stronger balance-sheet reassurance than the preview’s discussion of dividend coverage and acquisition funding risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $649 million cash and no debt,” and “remained in a positive net cash flow position even after funding the Granite Group acquisition in October.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the dividend payout, Granite cash outlay, and new credit facility as a “live catalyst,” asking for commentary on “payout, leverage, or capital allocation.”

surprises.description: Granite will add roughly $140–150 million of inventory to the balance sheet in October. The preview had highlighted management’s expectation for lower inventory in the second half, but did not account for this acquisition-related inventory addition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Granite Group acquisition adds…roughly $140–150 million of inventory joining the balance sheet in October.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “lower inventory in 2H26” and highlighted a clean Q3 inventory drawdown as supporting evidence.

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed a long-term gross-margin goal of 30%, above the current level, but cautioned that progress would be uneven quarter to quarter. The target is an encouraging longer-term ambition, while the warning tempers the expectation that margins will recover smoothly.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “reaffirmed a long-term gross margin goal of 30%, up from the current ~27% year-to-date level, while cautioning the path will be choppy quarter to quarter.”

surprises.description: The cost update was mixed against the preview’s expectation of expense leverage: fixed costs were restrained, but quarterly variable costs rose about 10% and technology spending rose about 13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fixed costs rose just 1% year-to-date (3% in the quarter) while variable costs rose 6% year-to-date (~10% in the quarter) and technology spending increased about 13% (~$6 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q2 SG&A was “+2% ex-acquisitions” and said to watch for leverage, with its base scenario assuming SG&A at 16.6% of sales.
